name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean after redistricting
Jerry Carl's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 3%
No polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean and a favorable national environment point strongly Republican, and Jerry Carl has raised over $1.1 million with more than $547,000 in outside support against a Democratic opponent with under $100,000. Markets price the race at roughly 95% Republican, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending surge for Clyde Jones could signal a closer race than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its R+17 partisan lean makes it strongly Republican terrain. Jerry Carl, the better-funded candidate, has raised about $1.16 million and holds a large cash advantage, with over $547,000 in outside spending backing him. Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $100,000 with no outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, money, and markets, all of which point the same way. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 3% chance. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
